## Where can agents be used in infectious disease modelling?

:::: {.sitem .teal}
**Many of the tasks often given to early career researchers**
::::

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="55%"}
::::: {.challenge-grid .where-grid}
:::: {.cbox .teal}
**Data**

- Pulling numbers out of reports, tables and figures
- Exploring data and making plots
- Generating hypotheses
::::
:::: {.cbox .slate}
**Models**

- Proposing candidate models and variations on them
- Optimising and differentiating model code
- Maths, such as analytical solutions
::::
:::: {.cbox .brick}
**Infrastructure**

- Checks that rerun whenever the model or data change
- Managing complex experimental workflows
::::
:::: {.cbox .grey}
**Thinking**

- Talking through model development
- A rubber duck that answers back
::::
:::::
:::
::: {.column width="45%"}
![](figures/agents-workflow-agents.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="The six-step workflow, question, data, model, fit, check and
report, with a tag over each. People over question; agents read and
digitise over data; people choose, agents write over model; agents,
every push over fit; agents run, people judge over check; agents draft,
people sign over report."}

![](figures/agents-rubber-duck.jpg){height="240px" fig-align="center"
fig-alt="A yellow rubber duck sitting beside a computer keyboard."}

::: {.attribution}

## How should we use the time agents free up?

:::: {.sitem .brick}
**What we could do.** More of the same work, faster
::::

![](figures/agents-time.png){height="500px" fig-align="center"

we should do leads to eight boxes, review, deep dives, big-picture thinking,
reducing technical debt, making work general and interoperable,
evaluating what works, collaboration, and talking to stakeholders."}

## How we use agents to develop EpiNow2

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="44%"}
::::: {.stack-grid}
:::: {.cbox .teal}
**What it is**

- Software we built to estimate how fast an outbreak is spreading, and
  to forecast it
- Public health agencies and other research groups use it
::::
:::: {.cbox .brick}
**The problem**

- Maintaining it is hard to fund through traditional research grants
::::
:::: {.cbox .slate}
**How agents help**

- Agents now propose most changes, and people check each one
::::
:::::

![](figures/agents-epinow2-prs.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Merged EpiNow2 changes per month from January 2025 to October
2026. Changes from people peak at about 20 a month in early 2025 and fall
to near zero from March 2026, as changes from agents rise to between 4
and 12 a month."}
:::
::: {.column width="56%"}
![](figures/agents-agent-2.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="A specification or a conversation leads to agents writing the
tasks, which feed a loop of read, write, run and check. Passing code
becomes a proposed change, which review agents send back into the loop
and we review. Merging refits the model and raises new tasks. The avatars
of seabbs-bot and sbfnk-bot sit by the loop as implementation agents, and
those of seabbs-review-bot and sbfnk-review-bot by the review agents.
Sam's photo sits by the specification and Seb's by the review."}

::: {.attribution}
Here Sam builds a feature and Seb reviews it. It also runs the other way
round ·
[EpiNow2](https://github.com/epiforecasts/EpiNow2), GitHub API, 2 November
2026 · e.g. [#1523](https://github.com/epiforecasts/EpiNow2/pull/1523),
[#1548](https://github.com/epiforecasts/EpiNow2/pull/1548) and
[#1552](https://github.com/epiforecasts/EpiNow2/pull/1552)
:::
:::

## Empirical Research Assistance for epidemic forecasting

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="45%"}
::::: {.stack-grid}
:::: {.cbox .teal}
**What it is**

- A language model writes many forecasting models, scores them and
  keeps the best
- It starts from models that forecasting teams already use
::::
:::: {.cbox .slate}
**What happened**

- Tested on past data, it seemed to beat the CDC's combined forecast
- Experts found the test had seen data that were corrected later
- Run live in 2025/26, it came first for flu, COVID-19 and RSV
::::
:::: {.cbox .brick}
**Why it matters**

- It builds on existing expertise
- Expert checks caught what the first test missed
- My guess is few groups could run 207,500 candidate models
::::
:::::
:::
::: {.column width="55%"}
![](figures/agents-martinson2026-fig2.png){width="100%"
fig-alt="Inputs of a problem statement, data, libraries and evaluation
requirements feed a tree of candidate models, each node coloured by its
score, with the best leaf circled and the forecasting code it produced,
an SIR model fitted with scipy, shown as the output."}

::: {.attribution}
Aygün et al. 2026,
[Nature](https://doi.org/10.1038/s41586-026-10658-6) ·
Bracher and Funk 2026,
[arXiv:2608.05883](https://arxiv.org/abs/2608.05883) ·
Martinson et al. 2026, Fig. 2,
[arXiv:2605.16238](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.16238)
:::
:::

## Estimating the size of the 2026 Bundibugyo virus outbreak

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width="40%"}
::::: {.stack-grid}
:::: {.cbox .teal}
**What it is**

- Situational awareness for the Ebola disease outbreak in the DRC
- One model fitted to all the surveillance streams in the public
  situation reports
- Estimates for each province and health zone
::::
:::: {.cbox .slate}
**What agents built**

- A replication of the first published estimate, the next day
- An interactive dashboard, with features added as users ask
- Forecast evaluation in real time
- Infrastructure to fit and check the model in public
::::
:::: {.cbox .brick}
**An experiment**

- Agent-driven outbreak modelling, meant as an external view
- It shows both the benefits and the dangers
::::
:::::
:::
::: {.column width="60%"}
![](figures/agents-bvd-dashboard.png){height="740px" fig-align="center"
fig-alt="An interactive map of health zones in north-eastern DRC shaded by
current reproduction number, beside a national panel with a reproduction
number of 1.01 and weekly confirmed cases with a seven-day forecast.
Below, the reproduction number falling from about 2 in May to about 1
from August, and four small maps of health-zone estimates."}

::: {.attribution}
McCabe et al. 2026, [doi:10.25560/130007](https://doi.org/10.25560/130007) ·
[BVDOutbreakSize report](https://epiforecasts.io/BVDOutbreakSize/dev/dashboard),
data to 25 October 2026
:::
